## Usage

Once installed, every command runs through the single `/impeccable` skill:

```
/impeccable audit        # Find issues
/impeccable polish       # Final cleanup
/impeccable distill      # Remove complexity
/impeccable critique     # Full design review
```

Type `/impeccable` alone to see the full command list.

Most commands accept an optional argument to focus on a specific area:

```
/impeccable audit the header
/impeccable polish the checkout form
```

If you reach for one command often, pin it with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as a standalone shortcut.

**Note:** Codex uses skills here, not `/prompts:` commands. Open `/skills` or type `$impeccable`. Repo-local installs live in `.agents/skills/`; user-wide installs live in `~/.agents/skills/`. GitHub Copilot uses `.github/skills/`. Restart the tool if a newly installed skill does not appear.

## Keeping `.impeccable` out of git

As you run commands, Impeccable writes working files under `.impeccable/`: critique and polish screenshots, live-mode session and preview state, runtime caches, and per-developer config. Most of it is ephemeral and should not be committed, while a few files are shared project artifacts that belong in the repo. Add this block to your project's `.gitignore`:

```gitignore
# impeccable-ignore-start
# Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
# The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
# Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
# design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
**/.impeccable/config.local.json
**/.impeccable/hook.cache.json
**/.impeccable/hook.pending.json
**/.impeccable/*.png
**/.impeccable/review/
**/.impeccable/questions/
**/.impeccable/live/server.json
**/.impeccable/live/sessions/
**/.impeccable/live/previews/
**/.impeccable/live/annotations/
**/.impeccable/live/cache/
**/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
**/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-events.jsonl
**/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-evidence/
**/.impeccable/live/pending-manual-edits.json
**/.impeccable/live/deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
**/.impeccable/live/*.png
# impeccable-ignore-end
```

The block is wrapped in `# impeccable-ignore-start` / `# impeccable-ignore-end` markers so you can recognize and refresh it later. The `**/` prefix makes each pattern match whether the active project's `.impeccable/` directory is at the repository root or under a nested workspace path like `apps/web/`.

**Keep these tracked** (they are shared project artifacts, do not add them to `.gitignore`):

- `.impeccable/config.json` (unified shared config)
- `.impeccable/live/config.json` (live-mode framework wiring)
- `.impeccable/design.json` (shared design spec)
- `.impeccable/surfaces/*.md` (route- or artifact-specific strategy and direction contracts)
- `.impeccable/critique/*.md` (review reports)

Impeccable also keeps its own `.gitignore` in the folders that hold decision-round state: `.impeccable/questions/` and `.impeccable/mocks/worlds/` ignore everything in them, and `.impeccable/build/` ignores `state.json`. That keeps new runtime files out of commits even in a project without the block above. A `.gitignore` cannot untrack a file git already tracks, though: when one of these files was committed earlier, the next roll prints a one-time notice with the fix, `git rm -r --cached .impeccable/questions` (plus any other folder it names), and writes its roll record to an untracked file until then.

If an ephemeral file (a screenshot, `config.local.json`) was committed before you added the block, `.gitignore` will not untrack it automatically. Run `git rm --cached <path>` to stop tracking it without deleting your local copy.

## Telemetry

When a new design starts, the skill asks the roll API at impeccable.style to deal a hand of visual worlds from the catalog. That request is the feature, so it always happens. Unless you opt out, it also feeds an anonymous record of which hand was shown and which card won, which is how the catalog learns what works.

What is sent, on the roll request and on the choice that follows it:

- the roll key (a random value per decision round), scope (direction or surface), visitor mode, and re-roll round
- the catalog revision the hand came from, and on the choice the kind of card that won (assigned, pick, challenger, canon, or a re-roll), its catalog id when a catalog world won, and its position on the page
- the client version, whether the choice came from the decision page or the agent, and a random id for that choice so a report sent twice is counted once

Never sent: your project's name, files, code, PRODUCT.md, or the names of the directions your agent wrote. Committed files such as surface briefs record only a seed reference, a hash of the roll key under a random salt kept in `~/.impeccable/seed-salt`, never the key itself. If no salt can be kept on a machine, the brief records no seed at all rather than a weaker hash. Roll keys are 128 random bits. If you pass your own short key with `--from`, its reference is easy to guess, so do not rely on it to keep that key private.

To turn it off, run `npx impeccable telemetry off` (stored in `~/.impeccable/config.json`), or set `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` or `IMPECCABLE_NO_TELEMETRY=1`. A project can opt everyone out with `"telemetry": false` in `.impeccable/config.json`. `npx impeccable telemetry status` shows the current state. Opted out, the roll still works and the API is told not to record it. Details: https://impeccable.style/privacy

## Design hook

On Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor, and Grok Build, `npx impeccable install` and `npx impeccable update` install a provider-native hook manifest along with the skill payload. The hook runs the Impeccable design detector on direct UI file edits and surfaces findings back into the agent flow. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, and Cursor surface findings after the edit (and run a deeper pass on Stop where supported). Grok Build scans after the edit to warm Stop, then surfaces on Stop; PostToolUse stdout never reaches the model.

Installed hook surfaces:

- Claude Code: `.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored, machine-local) runs `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook`. A hook moved into the shared `settings.json` is honored in place.
- GitHub Copilot: `.github/hooks/impeccable.json` (committed, shared by the Copilot CLI and the cloud agent) runs `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook`. The Copilot CLI activates it once the file is on the repository's default branch and the folder is trusted.
- Cursor: `.cursor/hooks.json` runs `.cursor/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook` on `postToolUse` for file writes. Projects set up with the older `preToolUse` write gate keep working; `npx impeccable update` moves them to the post-edit hook.
- Codex: `.codex/hooks.json` runs `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook`, with a `commandWindows` sibling that calls `impeccable.cmd` for cmd.exe.
- Grok Build: `.grok/hooks/impeccable.json` runs `.grok/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook`. Requires `/hooks-trust` or `--trust`. Findings reach the model on Stop, not after each edit.
- Hermes Agent: the `impeccable-design-hook` plugin in `~/.hermes/plugins/` runs the skill's launcher on `write_file` and `patch` results and on `pre_verify` before the turn ends. Hermes plugins are opt-in, so run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once.

Every command goes through the launcher shipped in the skill's `scripts/` directory (`impeccable`, or `impeccable.cmd` on Windows), guarded so a missing launcher is a silent no-op. The launcher runs the engine binary that ships next to it, or downloads the pinned version once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`. No Node or other runtime is required for the hook or the skill.

In Claude Code, installed command hooks run independently of model-tool approval. The first edit or Stop event can therefore download and cache the engine even if the session denies the model's launcher command. Review installed hooks before unattended runs; to disable all Claude Code hooks for a run, pass `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'`. See [Claude Code's hook security guidance](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#security-considerations).

The installer preserves unrelated hook entries and settings. If a hook manifest is malformed, install/update aborts by default; rerun with `--force` to back up the malformed file as `.bak` and replace it.

On an interactive `install`/`update`, Impeccable explains the hook and offers to install it (default yes). Your choice is remembered per-developer in the gitignored `.impeccable/config.local.json`, so you are not asked again; `--no-hooks` skips it for that run without recording anything. Hook lifecycle settings live under the `hook` key of `.impeccable/config.json`; detector ignores live under `detector`, shared by `/impeccable hooks` and `npx impeccable detect`.

For debugging, set `hook.auditLog` in `.impeccable/config.json` to a path (or the legacy `IMPECCABLE_HOOK_LOG` env var) to write one NDJSON line per hook invocation. Leave it unset for normal use.

## Build path: comp-first or code-first

When a new surface gets designed, Impeccable either generates a full-fidelity comp first and builds to match it, or builds straight in code with the ambition written into a development-only direction contract in the surface brief and checked at the finish. Comp-first composes bolder and takes longer; code-first is leaner and faster. The choice covers landing pages and showcase surfaces. App screens and documents are built code-first either way, because they come out better built than pictured. `/impeccable init` asks once and records the answer as `buildPath` in `.impeccable/config.json`:

```json
{ "buildPath": "comp" }
```

The values are `comp` and `code`, and nothing else is read. Set it in the gitignored `.impeccable/config.local.json` to override the team's committed value on one machine, which is what you want when your harness has no image generation. In a monorepo, commit it once at the repo root and any workspace that wants something else sets its own. The choice appears at all only where image generation is available, since without it there is nothing to comp.

You do not have to re-run `init` to set it on a project that predates the setting, and you do not have to edit the file by hand either. Whatever is recorded is a default rather than a lock: every decision page carries a footer toggle, and flipping it binds that session only. Flip it on a project that has recorded nothing and Impeccable asks once, after the round, whether to keep it, then writes your answer. That is the whole migration path for an existing project: use the toggle when the default is wrong, and answer the question that follows.

Codex requires one platform step that Impeccable cannot safely skip: open `/hooks` after install or update and approve the project hook. There is no Codex marketplace/plugin install flow for this hook.

Full hook docs: [impeccable.style/docs/hooks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks).

The Stop pass suppresses confirmed pre-existing findings when a verified before-edit baseline is available (currently Claude Edit/Write results for text scans). Other findings are marked new or attribution unknown; unknown is not evidence that your session caused the problem. Explicit `detect` scans remain unchanged.

Manual copy commands are fallback/debug instructions. The normal path is:

```bash
npx impeccable install
npx impeccable update
```

## Live mode and production sites

Live mode edits a local checkout through a development server or local static HTML. Injecting its localhost HTTP helper into a deployed production site, including an HTTPS site, is not supported. Do not disable browser security or weaken production CSP to make it work.

Use live mode only in projects you trust to run locally. Applying copy edits automatically runs `package.json`'s optional `scripts["impeccable:manual-edit-validate"]` command in a shell, with your user permissions; review that script before using live mode in an unfamiliar checkout.

For production inspection, use `npx impeccable detect https://example.com` or the browser extension. These inspect the rendered page; they do not provide live variant editing or write changes back to your source.

## CLI

Impeccable includes a standalone CLI for detecting anti-patterns without an AI harness. `npx impeccable` is a small shim that runs the same engine binary the skill uses (installed as a platform-specific optional dependency, or fetched once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`); Node is needed only for `npx` itself, and you can also download the binary directly and put it on your PATH.

```bash
npx impeccable detect src/                   # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect index.html             # scan an HTML file
npx impeccable detect https://example.com    # scan a URL (uses an installed Chrome, Chromium, or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json .               # CI-friendly JSON output
npx impeccable detect --github src/          # GitHub Actions annotations on stdout
npx impeccable detect --list-rules           # catalog of detector rule ids, names, and descriptions
npx impeccable detect --no-config src/       # raw scan, ignoring project config/context
npx impeccable ignores list                  # show detector ignores
npx impeccable ignores add-file "src/legacy/**"
npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"
```

The detector catches 62 deterministic issues across AI slop (side-tab borders, purple gradients, bounce easing, dark glows) and general design quality (line length, cramped padding, small touch targets, skipped headings, and more).

Human-readable findings are diagnostics written to stderr, so redirect them with `2> findings.txt`. Use `--json` for machine-readable results on stdout, or `--github` for GitHub Actions annotations (one workflow command per finding). GitHub displays at most 10 annotations of each type per step and 50 per job, and the rest stay in the log; findings from the HTML engine may carry no line number, so they annotate the file. `--list-rules` prints the detector catalog to stdout and does not scan. Exit `0` means the scan completed without primary findings, exit `2` means it completed with primary findings, and exit `1` means at least one requested target could not be scanned; operational failure takes precedence for a partial multi-target scan. URL scans inspect the rendered DOM, computed layout, and accessible linked stylesheets; browser security still prevents reading cross-origin CSS without CORS. A clean detector run is evidence, not proof of visual or accessibility quality: it does not replace inspecting the rendered experience across relevant viewports.

By default, `detect` respects the same `.impeccable/config.json` and `.impeccable/config.local.json` detector config as the design hook: `detector.ignoreRules`, `detector.ignoreFiles`, `detector.ignoreValues`, and `detector.designSystem.enabled`. Hook lifecycle settings such as `hook.enabled` only affect automatic hook execution.

For a waiver that should travel with one file instead of the repo config, add an inline comment in the file: `<!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc -->`. The marker works in any comment syntax, scopes to the whole file (or one line with `impeccable-disable-line` / `impeccable-disable-next-line`), and is bypassed by `--no-inline-ignores` or `--no-config`.

Full detector docs: [impeccable.style/docs/detector](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector).

Add your list afterwards and the next person with your model skips that step: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Doing it by hand Everything the assistant does, you can run yourself. The tools need Python 3 and nothing else. `tools/tv.py` talks to network ADB on port 5555. If that port stays closed and the TV offers Wireless debugging with a pairing code (the Chromecast with Google TV and the Google TV Streamer do), pair it once with the stock `adb` and run `adb tcpip 5555` first, as [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#connecting) describes. ```bash python3 -m venv tools/venv && tools/venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements.txt export TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 # your TV's IP address tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --probe # model, Android version, firmware tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py 'pm list packages' # one shell command on the TV tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # apply a debloat list tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # undo it, stock launcher back tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/check.py examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # what a firmware update undid TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 launcher/build-and-install.sh # build the launcher and make it Home tools/theme.sh themes/aurora # push a theme; --reset removes it ``` | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | [`tools/tv.py`](tools/tv.py) | Pure-Python ADB client: shell, batch, push, pull, reboot, and screenshots, optionally pressing remote keys first. Works where the stock `adb` binary is blocked. Optional [paired Google ADB backend](tools/native-adb.md) for encrypted Wireless debugging. | | [`tools/b64push.py`](tools/b64push.py) | Uploads large files such as APKs in base64 chunks and verifies the checksum. | | [`tools/relay.py`](tools/relay.py) | Forwards a local port to the TV's ADB port, for assistants whose sandbox can't reach your network. Listens on this computer only. [Guide](tools/relay.md). | | [`tools/disable.sh`](tools/disable.sh), [`restore.sh`](tools/restore.sh) | Apply or undo a debloat list, the undo from the state recorded before the change. | | [`tools/recovery.py`](tools/recovery.py) | Writes the record `disable.sh` needs to undo itself, and prints the restore batch. | | [`tools/check.py`](tools/check.py) | Compares the TV with the list that was applied, for what a firmware update undid; `--fix` puts it back. | | [`tools/adb-closed.py`](tools/adb-closed.py) | Checks that the TV's network ADB port is closed once debugging is off: exits 0 when the TV refuses the connection, 1 while it is still open, 2 when nothing answered or the check itself could not run. No `nc` needed. | | [`tools/privacy.py`](tools/privacy.py) | Audits the TV for voice, ACR and telemetry candidates and prints the evidence for each; `--write` turns the findings into a list `disable.sh` and `restore.sh` already understand. | | [`tools/theme.sh`](tools/theme.sh), [`theme_restart.py`](tools/theme_restart.py) | Push a folder from [`themes/`](themes/) to the launcher and restart Home. | | [`tools/manage.py`](tools/manage.py) | List every add-on, theme and switch with its screenshot, see what is on the TV, and install, update or remove one by running its creator's own script. | | [`tools/bench.py`](tools/bench.py) | Measures the launcher that answers HOME: key latency, how far the focus moved, janky frames, cold start, return to Home, and the idle CPU and PSS it costs. Changes nothing on the TV and writes the raw per-key numbers to JSON; no extra install. | | [`tools/trace.py`](tools/trace.py), [`trace_report.py`](tools/trace_report.py) | Records Perfetto traces of the launcher (return to Home, cold start, D-pad) and reports where its time goes, per run and before against after. Optional: needs [`requirements-perf.txt`](tools/requirements-perf.txt). [Guide](tools/trace.md). | | [`tools/flamechart.py`](tools/flamechart.py) | Draws a before/after flame chart from those traces, for a pull request: one lane per thread on a shared time scale, the work a change targets in magenta with its total. Optional, like the trace tools. [Guide](tools/flamechart.md). | | [`tools/screendiff.py`](tools/screendiff.py) | Compares a before and an after screenshot pixel by pixel, leaving out the clock or anything you mask, and writes the pair with your Wi-Fi name blurred. Optional, like the trace tools. [Guide](tools/screendiff.md). | | [`tools/race_calendar.py`](tools/race_calendar.py) | Writes this season's F1 calendar into a theme for race-weekend mode, from the free Jolpica API. | | [`launcher/build-and-install.sh`](launcher/build-and-install.sh) | Builds a shrunk release (about 532 KB), installs it, switches Home, and rolls back if Home does not land on it. | The scripts never leave the TV without a Home app: they only disable a stock launcher they recognise, and skip the Home app in a list until another launcher answers HOME. Your own lists can live outside the repository: list paths are relative to the directory you run from, and absolute paths work too.
Windows (PowerShell) Every script has a PowerShell twin next to it. On Windows with Android Studio installed nothing else is needed: ```powershell python -m venv tools\venv; tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r tools\requirements.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File launcher\build-and-install.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\disable.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 examples\xiaomi-mi-tv-4a\debloat.txt ```
How the scripts protect Home The install scripts ask the TV which launcher owns Home and only disable one they recognise, the four in `KNOWN_STOCK_LAUNCHERS`: `com.google.android.tvlauncher`, `com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx`, `com.google.android.leanbacklauncher` and Xiaomi's `com.mitv.tvhome` (PatchWall). Pass `STOCK_LAUNCHER=` (`-StockLauncher`) to override, or `none` to leave it alone. `tools/disable.sh` (`disable.ps1`) applies the same rule before it disables anything: - If the list contains the app that owns Home and no other app on the TV answers HOME, it skips that entry, says why, and disables the rest of the list. So a list applied before the launcher handover cannot leave the TV with nothing to start. - The setup wizard, the settings apps, a vendor `FallbackHome` and factory-test apps (Xiaomi's `com.duokan.factorytest`) answer HOME too and don't count. - On Google TV it also keeps the owner while setupwraith answers HOME and stays enabled (not listed, or kept for the Wi-Fi network): setupwraith answers ahead of an installed launcher that is not Home yet, so it would take Home. Run the same list again once `launcher/build-and-install.sh` has made the new launcher Home and the entry is applied; `FORCE_HOME=1` (`$env:FORCE_HOME`) disables it anyway.
## The microphone, and what can be said about it "Which of these packages is listening?" has no honest one-line answer: a permission scan shows fifty system packages with `RECORD_AUDIO` that record nothing, and ACR clients see the screen with no audio permission at all. [`tools/privacy.py`](tools/privacy.py) reports what the TV actually says, with the evidence for each voice, ACR and telemetry candidate: `TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/privacy.py`, and `--write` turns them into a normal debloat list. What the audit cannot do is prove intent: [docs/privacy.md](docs/privacy.md) explains why. ## The launcher A small native home screen for Android TV: **about 532 KB**, plain Java, built for TVs with 1 GB of RAM. No blur, no video, no network permission, no background services. The **TV** needs Android 8.0 (API 26) or newer, the `minSdk` in [`launcher/app/build.gradle`](launcher/app/build.gradle); what is left on an older set is in [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). | What | How it works | |---|---| | **Configure** | Dock order, hidden apps, Live TV app, 4 to 7 tiles per row, reduced motion. All in [`config.xml`](launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml) | | **Settings on the TV** | Hold OK on Settings for launcher settings. Optional `launcher_settings_button` makes a normal click open them directly; TV settings remain on the settings page and their app tile. | | **Themes** | Background, wallpaper and layout from a `config.json` pushed over Wi-Fi, no rebuild. ten ship in [`themes/`](themes/), the built-in `default/` included | | **29 languages** | Follows the TV's language, with a fully mirrored right-to-left layout for Hebrew | | **App library** | Optional: browse every installed app and add or remove Home shortcuts. See [the app library guide](docs/app-library.md) | | **Tile menu** | Optional (`tile_menu`): hold OK on a tile for Move, Remove from Home and App info. Off, holding OK opens App info | | **Module cards** | Any TV app can offer its own tile; you approve each one once. See [`docs/modules.md`](docs/modules.md) | | **Add-ons** | Optional apps that plug in as module cards, kept in [`addons/`](addons/) and never built into the launcher | | **Clock screensaver** | A drifting clock over the glow, so nothing burns in | | **Remote keys** | Keeps the Input, YouTube and gear buttons working after the stock launcher is gone | Themes, switches and add-ons together, with screenshots: [cleanyour.tv/addons](https://cleanyour.tv/addons). **More:** [docs/launcher.md](docs/launcher.md) has the launcher settings page row by row, changing the default home, the languages, remote keys, the Clock screensaver, navigation and building it yourself. ## Restoring your TV Keep the list you applied. One line puts the TV back the way it was: ```bash TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/restore.sh examples//debloat.txt # Android TV TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/restore.sh examples//debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx # Google TV ``` | What | How | |---|---| | **A record comes first** | Before `tools/disable.sh` changes anything it writes down what the TV looked like, in `~/.cleanyourtv/`. | | **Restore replays it** | A package you had disabled yourself stays disabled, and Home goes back to the component that owned it. | | **The launcher stays installed** | Remove it from the TV's Settings → Apps if you want it gone. | | **No computer?** | If the TV is unreachable, its own Settings → Apps page can re-enable packages too. | **More:** [docs/restore.md](docs/restore.md) has what the record holds, when the stock launcher argument counts, and what happens without a record. ## After a firmware update An update installs over the cleaned-up system: the listed packages come back, Home goes to the stock launcher, and new preloads appear that no list mentions. Open ADB again as in [Quick start](#quick-start) step 1, then compare the TV with the list you applied; `--fix` puts it back: ```bash TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/check.py examples//debloat.txt ``` **More:** [docs/firmware-updates.md](docs/firmware-updates.md) has the exit codes, a weekly check, what `--fix` changes, TVs that keep the stock launcher as Home, and lists that disable the updater. ## When something goes wrong The full list of things that bit us is in [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). The three that matter most: - 🍎 **macOS blocks `adb connect`** ("No route to host") under Local Network privacy. `tools/tv.py` avoids the binary. - ⚠️ **Disable the stock launcher only after the new one is installed and running**, or Home lands on a factory test app. The install script orders this for you. - 🔁 **On Google TV the setup wizard** (`com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith`) can take Home and crash-loop the system after the stock launcher is disabled. Disable it too, and list it in your `debloat.txt` so restore brings it back. - But check `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'` first: if the Wi-Fi network was saved during setup it belongs to setupwraith, and disabling it deletes the network (re-join it in Settings first; `tools/disable.sh` skips setupwraith until you do). - On Google's own Chromecast and on the Google TV Streamer it also costs phone casting, see [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). - Stuck already? `tools/tv.py 'pm enable --user 0 com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx'`. ## Questions people ask
I don't code and don't have a laptop. Can I still do this? Yes. [@udhaykumarbala](https://github.com/udhaykumarbala) built a free, open-source [phone app](https://cleanyour.tv/app) for Android that does the same cleanup over Wi-Fi: it connects to the TV, shows a plan first, saves a restore point, and only switches apps off, so everything can be put back. It's community-built.
Is this safe? Can it brick the TV? Nothing is flashed, rooted or deleted; packages are disabled in the user profile. The risk is disabling something the TV leans on, which is why lists are applied in small batches with a restore script ready. The TV's own Settings → Apps page can re-enable packages even without the tools. If the TV no longer starts far enough for that, a factory reset from its recovery menu is usually the way back. More: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md#is-this-safe-can-it-brick-the-tv)
What about firmware updates? The updater is left on in most lists, so firmware updates arrive as usual. Some lists disable the TV's own updater, and on those a firmware update arrives only when you re-enable it. When one does land it installs over the cleaned-up system, so a package comes back and you re-run the script: see [After a firmware update](#after-a-firmware-update).
Won't the apps break? Streaming apps still update through the Play Store, which is left alone. The launcher just lists what is installed and launches it with intents that have been stable for a decade.
Can I do this for someone in another home? Yes, over a private [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com) link instead of the same Wi-Fi: either Tailscale on their TV, shared with you, or a computer or Apple TV at their home routing to it. Never by opening the ADB port on their router. Step by step in [docs/REMOTE.md](docs/REMOTE.md).
Isn't ADB access a security hole? It is one explicit "allow this computer" tap on the TV, the same as developing an Android app. Network ADB is plaintext on port 5555, and on some firmware any device on the LAN gets a shell, so close it when you are done: 1. On the TV: Developer options → turn **USB debugging**, **Network/ADB debugging** and **Wireless debugging** off, whichever the TV has, and revoke the USB debugging authorisations. 2. Reboot the TV, then confirm the port is gone from your computer: `python3 tools/adb-closed.py ` must say the port is closed. The launcher keeps working without debugging. More, including checking Wireless debugging's own port: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md#isnt-adb-access-a-security-hole)
Can it block ads inside apps too? Partly, with Android's Private DNS (Android 9 and newer). Point it at an ad-blocking resolver such as [AdGuard DNS](https://adguard-dns.io) and every app's ad and tracker domains stop resolving, system-wide, surviving reboots. The trade-off: that resolver then sees every DNS query the TV makes, and it does not remove YouTube ads. More, with the two commands and how to switch back: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md#can-it-block-ads-inside-apps-too)
Are there switches in the TV's own Settings worth flipping too? A few, and they need no ADB: the advertising ID, Location, Usage & diagnostics and Scanning always available, plus Apps only mode where the stock launcher stays. Flip Usage & diagnostics before the debloat; on some TVs its page goes with it. More, with the paths for Google TV, Android TV and Fire OS: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md#are-there-switches-in-the-tvs-own-settings-worth-flipping-too)
AirPlay? Not from this repo. Chromecast built-in stays for Android phones. For iPhones, [jqssun/android-airplay-server](https://github.com/jqssun/android-airplay-server) works; an install script for it is in [PR #84](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv/pull/84).
Can I just download the APK? Build it with the one-line script; it takes a minute and you control what goes on your TV. No prebuilt binaries.
## The story On 17 October 2026 I posted [a before and after](https://x.com/gathint/status/2111379569030939102) of my parents' TV, cleaned up by Claude Code over Wi-Fi. It reached 7.4M views, people started doing the same to their own TVs, and their replies turned into the lists here: 170+ TV models from 200+ contributors in four days. The repo was called tv-vibehack until the 19th; old links work. The coverage since is in [docs/PRESS.md](docs/PRESS.md). ## Contributing The most useful contribution is your TV's debloat list, so the next person with that model does not have to rediscover it. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the format and the testing we ask for. Contributing through a coding agent? [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) gives it the same rules. | How to help | What it means | |---|---| | **Your TV's debloat list** | The most useful one: the next person with that model skips the discovery. | | **Launcher and prompt** | Launcher improvements and sharper prompt wording are welcome too. | | **Built something on top?** | A launcher, a port, a theme: add it to [SHOWCASE.md](SHOWCASE.md), where a hundred and forty-four projects already live, sorted into home screens, forks, add-ons, tools and other platforms, with an index by TV brand. | The people whose work is in this repo:

# ub-mode

`ub-mode` is an agent skill that enforces disciplined software engineering principles when writing or changing code. It is loosely based on portions of [@poteto](https://github.com/poteto)'s rules (`poteto-mode` / `pstack`), reduced and paired with deterministic quality-gate tools:

1. **First Make it Work** — Laziness Protocol, Foundational Thinking, TDD, Redesign From First Principles, Attack the Premise, Subtract Before You Add, Outcome-Oriented Execution, Build the Lever, and Architecture (Model the Domain, Boundary Discipline, Type System Discipline, Make Operations Idempotent, Separate Before Serializing Shared State).
2. **Then Make it Right** — Fix Root Causes, Sequence Work into Verifiable Units, Test Behavior (Not Implementation), [Crapper](https://github.com/unclebob/crapper) (`CRAP < 10`), [Dryer](https://github.com/unclebob/dryer) (duplication `< 0.8`), [Mutator](https://github.com/unclebob/mutator) (cover the uncovered, kill the survivors, delete dead code), and Refactoring.
3. **Practice** — Keep a Log, Guard the Context Window, Worktree Cleanup, and Commit and Push in small ordered commits.

## Companion Tool Repositories

`ub-mode` relies on deterministic quality-gate tools to enforce structure, complexity, duplication, and test thoroughness:

- [unclebob/crapper](https://github.com/unclebob/crapper) — Computes cyclomatic complexity, test coverage, and CRAP score per function so every function stays under the CRAP threshold (`< 10`).
- [unclebob/dryer](https://github.com/unclebob/dryer) — Detects structural code duplication so duplicate blocks (`>= 0.8` similarity) are eliminated.
- [unclebob/mutator](https://github.com/unclebob/mutator) — Runs mutation testing to expose uncovered code and surviving mutants that tests fail to catch.
- [unclebob/uml-viewer](https://github.com/unclebob/uml-viewer) — Visualizes components, coverage, CRAP, mutation scores, and dependency directions.

## Installation

Copy `SKILL.md` into your agent's skills directory as `ub-mode/SKILL.md` (for example `~/.grok/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`, `~/.claude/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`, or `~/.cursor/skills/ub-mode/SKILL.md`), then invoke `/ub-mode`.

# Hallmark **A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated.** [usehallmark.com](https://www.usehallmark.com)  ·  fifty themes  ·  custom on request  ·  redesign and audit by name Made by Together AI.

Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of fifty materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an email sign-up at the end of every page, a form that says thanks without sending anything. A fresh-context reviewer gets the last word. The gates come in tiers. The **Floor** never ships (contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, a broken phone layout). **Reflex** gates are the defaults a model falls into; a build with a reason may overrule one on the record. **Finish** checks are craft detail that never blocks a ship. ## New in v2 - **Fifty themes.** Each is a material (paper, type, colour, surfaces, its own components and texture) with a picture of a finished page, and the build lays out its own page in it. - **Built from the job.** A booking page books, a shop sells, a newsletter subscribes: the action sits where the category puts it, and the page ends on it. - **Custom.** Ask for a custom page and Hallmark designs from your prompt alone, under the same rules and checks. - **Your real product.** Point it at a URL, a dev server or an app and it captures the screenshots itself. - **Real photographs.** 755 openly licensed photos, picked per subject and credited on the page. - **Redesign and audit.** `/hallmark redesign ` rebuilds a page and keeps its content and wiring; `/hallmark audit ` only reports. ## Themes
Dusk
Closewise, bank reconciliation		 Cobalt
Relay, a webhook API		 Studio
Field Office, an identity studio		 Atelier
Maison Orla, a fragrance atelier		 Ribbon
Lull, a sleep sounds app
Furrow
Fieldbook, farm records		 Dose
Tandem, a family medication app		 Refract
Bellwater Lido, an outdoor pool		 Vantage
Swath, construction site scans		 Hedgerow
Five Mile Gin, a distillery
Ten of the fifty. A theme is a material, not a plan: it never says what a page contains or in what order, so two prompts in one theme make two different pages. Each is one file of at most 8 KB in [`references/themes/`](skills/hallmark/references/themes/) with a picture beside it; a build reads exactly one. See them all at [usehallmark.com](https://www.usehallmark.com). ## Custom Say **custom** and Hallmark drops the themes: no plan, no components, no palette recipe, only the floor, the gates and a short direction in [`direction.md`](skills/hallmark/references/direction.md) to find one idea that only this client has and let it run the page. ## How a build runs 1. Pre-flight reads the project (fonts, palette, framework, a locked `design.md`) and asks once for the material: photos, screenshots, real numbers. Nothing is invented. 2. `scripts/theme.mjs deal` offers three themes that fit the prompt and clear the log; `draw` deals the page's anatomy from its job. 3. The hero is built alone, rendered and reviewed cold before the rest of the page exists. 4. `scripts/sloplint.mjs --render` checks the page at eight widths, then a subagent reviews it with fresh eyes. Each page is self-contained HTML and CSS, stamped in its first CSS comment with the decisions it took. ## Redesign Hallmark never starts on a design that already exists unless you name it: ``` /hallmark redesign ./src/app /hallmark audit ./index.html ``` A full redesign keeps the content and the wiring and changes the system and the layout; say *keep the layout* for a restyle or *polish* for only the tells. `sloplint --before` records every link, field, handler and heading first, `sloplint --kept` fails the redesign if one went missing, and the handoff is a side-by-side before and after. ## Install ``` npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g ``` `-g` installs for every project; leave it off to install into the current one. Needs Node 18 or later. The browser checks (`sloplint --render`, screenshots) also need `npm i -g puppeteer-core` and Chrome; without them the static checks still run. | Harness | Lands in | Invoke | | --- | --- | --- | | Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/hallmark` | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Codex CLI | `~/.agents/skills/hallmark` | `$hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Cursor | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | OpenCode | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | - **One harness only:** `npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g --agent claude-code` (or `codex`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `github-copilot`). - **As a Claude Code plugin:** `/plugin marketplace add nutlope/hallmark`, then `/plugin install hallmark@hallmark` (invoked as `/hallmark:hallmark`). - **From a clone:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/install.mjs` validates every theme and reference before it copies; `install-hook.mjs` adds an edit-time Floor check to Claude Code. - **Lint any page:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/sloplint.mjs --render`. - **If it does not fire on its own,** name it: *use hallmark to build ...*. ## Inspired by [Impeccable](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable) · [frontend-design](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/frontend-design) · [Open Design](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design) · [Kami](https://github.com/tw93/kami) · [taste-skill](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill) · [huashu-design](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-design) · [UI UX Pro Max](https://github.com/nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill) · [Emil Kowalski's skills](https://github.com/emilkowalski/skills) · [Web Interface Guidelines](https://github.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines) ## Licence MIT. Use it, fork it, ship it. The photo library (`skills/hallmark/scripts/photos.json`) lists photographs hosted on Wikimedia Commons and holds no image files. Each keeps its own licence (CC0, public domain, CC BY or CC BY-SA), and Hallmark credits every one it uses on the page. It does not use stock sites (Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay), whose terms bar AI tools from picking their images.

# AI Design Skills A growing collection of design skills for AI coding tools — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and anything else that reads a markdown rules file. Each skill is a self-contained folder. Install the ones you need. --- ## Skills | Skill | What it does | |---|---| | [`landing-page-design`](./skills/landing-page-design/SKILL.md) | Builds a landing page from scratch — intake questions, page structure, conversion copy, plus a full visual system (type, spacing, radius, motion) | More on the way. [Upgrading an existing site instead of building new?](https://github.com/elayadesign/redesign-skill) That one lives in its own repo since it predates this collection. --- ## Install Pick a skill from the table above, then swap `` below for its folder name.
Claude Code ```bash mkdir -p .claude/skills git clone https://github.com/elayadesign/ai-design-skills.git /tmp/ai-design-skills cp -r /tmp/ai-design-skills/skills/ .claude/skills/ ``` Then just ask, in plain language, for what that skill covers.
Cursor ```bash mkdir -p .cursor/rules curl -o .cursor/rules/.md \ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elayadesign/ai-design-skills/main/skills//SKILL.md ``` Or paste the file into **Settings → Rules for AI**.
Codex / Windsurf / other Copy the skill's `SKILL.md` into whatever your tool uses for project rules: | Tool | Path | |---|---| | Codex | `AGENTS.md` | | Windsurf | `.windsurfrules` | | Cline | `.clinerules` | | Generic | paste into your system prompt |
Claude.ai (no terminal) Download the skill's `SKILL.md` and upload it to a Project, or attach it to a chat and say *"follow this."*
--- ## Make it yours Every skill's design values (fonts, colors, spacing, motion) live in one section near the bottom of its file. Fork this repo, edit that section, and the rest of the skill follows automatically. --- ## Credits `landing-page-design` adapts content realism and motion ideas from [Leonxlnx/taste-skill](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill) by Leon Lin, MIT licensed. Details are at the end of [its SKILL.md](./skills/landing-page-design/SKILL.md#credits). --- ## License MIT. Use it, fork it, ship it, sell what you build with it. No attribution needed.

items.readme_text:
Design with an elephant. Review with a goldfish.

Install  ·  Quickstart  ·  Documentation  ·  Website


Thousands of Google engineers use EGM, an open-source plugin, to draft specs with deep-context agents and stress-test them with zero-context subagents before writing code. **Elephant** holds your project context and drafts the specification. **Goldfish** reviewers examine the draft and referenced source material without the earlier conversation, helping expose unstated assumptions and blind spots. **You** make the architectural trade-offs and approve the specification before implementing. Use it when a feature needs design decisions before implementation. For a small, clear bug fix, use your normal coding workflow. ## Install Choose your coding agent. Install the complete plugin so its skills can read the reviewer prompts and document standards. ### Antigravity ```sh agy plugin install https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model ``` ### Claude Code ```sh claude plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model claude plugin install egm@egm ``` ### Codex ```sh codex plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model codex plugin add egm@egm ``` Start a new session after installation. For **Claude Cowork** and **ChatGPT Work**, see the [setup guide](docs/harnesses.md). ## Try your first design Open your project in your coding agent and choose a feature that needs design decisions. This example adds webhook delivery: what should happen when a delivery fails, or the same event arrives twice? The commands below are shown without a prefix. In Antigravity (agy CLI) and Claude Code, add the `/egm:` prefix, for example `/egm:egm-brainstorm`. In Codex, select the corresponding EGM skill from the skill picker. Brainstorming and review require a session that can create fresh subagents. **Explore the idea** ```text /egm-brainstorm Add webhook delivery to this project. ``` Discuss requirements and trade-offs with the agent. Fresh reviewers challenge the proposal, and the agent saves the agreed direction in `concepts_brief.md`. **Draft the specification** ```text /egm-draft ``` The agent turns the brief into `design_draft.md`, pausing after each section for your feedback in chat. **Review the draft** ```text /egm-review design_draft.md ``` Use the draft path returned by the agent. Fresh reviewers check the design, its clarity, its fit with the code, and its implementation plan. Choose which findings to address. When you approve the design, ask your coding agent to implement it. See the [workflow guide](docs/getting_started.md) for the full process, including saving approved specifications under `docs/designs/`. ## How it works
RoleContextResponsibility
ElephantYour project, requirements, and earlier decisionsExplore the problem and draft the specification.
GoldfishThe document and its referenced source material, without the earlier conversationFind missing assumptions, unclear requirements, and implementation risks.
YouThe goals and constraints that matterResolve trade-offs, approve the design, and decide what to build.
Goldfish reviews require fresh subagent contexts. If your agent cannot create them, EGM stops the review. A review does not replace tests or human judgment. See [supported environments and verification limits](docs/harnesses.md#support-status--contributing-other-harnesses). ## Choose a skill You can use each skill when you need it. You do not have to follow the full sequence.
SkillUse it to…
 BrainstormTest an idea and write a concept brief.
 DraftTurn a brief or existing notes into a design document.
 ResolveWork through review findings and agree on changes.
 BootstrapCreate or update documentation for an existing codebase.
 ReviewReview a design with fresh agents across five stages.
 Review loopRun a configured group of reviewers for a specific review task.
 Drift reportCompare checked-in documents with the current source code.
## Learn more - [Getting started](docs/getting_started.md): the workflow and project layout. - [Setup](docs/harnesses.md): installation, agent capabilities, and known limits. - [Architecture](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/docs/designs/architecture.md): how skills and reviewers fit together. - [Testing](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/TESTING.md): checks, execution records, and verification limits. - [Dave Rensin’s original essay](https://medium.com/@drensin/elephants-goldfish-and-the-new-golden-age-of-software-engineering-c33641a48874): the ideas behind EGM. ## Contribute Read [contributing](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for PRs, [issues](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues) for bugs, and [discussions](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/discussions) for questions. ## License [Apache 2.0](LICENSE). This is not an officially supported Google product.
